data.name: Forgotten Tales: Day of the Dead
data.detailed_description:
There is an old legend in Mexico that on “Dia de los Muertos” the Day of the Dead, the gates of heaven will open and the souls of our loved ones can visit the land of the living. That’s where the story of Manuel and Maria begins. An evil soul has kidnapped Maria. And now Manuel asks for your help to join him in this incredible adventure through the land of the dead after his beloved bride. Journey through beautiful scenery, relaxing music and help funny characters to find their belongings. Prove your skills in this challenging solitaire game!

Steam Trading Cards

Features

  • tons of unique and clever puzzles
  • a compelling story of love
  • a rich and vibrant world
  • tough challenges and great rewards

What people say about Forgotten Tales


What a fantastic solitaire game, it even has a fantastic story to go along with it.
I loved the features, the graphics, and the Solitaire game, but most of all, it has a very interesting story, enjoy! - pennmom36, Big Fish Games

I love this solitaire game! It’s colorful, the characters are funny the story line is cute. It’s different than most of the other solitaire games which can get repetitive and therefore boring. I would recommend this game. - Mernon54, Big Fish Games

reviews.review:
Forgotten Tales: Day of the Dead is a relaxing solitaire adventure developed and published by Green Sauce Games that blends traditional card gameplay with a colorful story inspired by the spirit of the Day of the Dead celebration. Instead of presenting a simple collection of solitaire boards, the game builds a lighthearted fantasy adventure around Manuel, who embarks on a dangerous journey through the realm of the dead after the woman he loves, Maria, is taken away by a sinister force. This narrative gives players a meaningful reason to progress beyond simply completing card layouts, turning each victory into another step toward rescuing Maria while uncovering charming locations and meeting unusual inhabitants of the afterlife.

At its heart, the gameplay follows the familiar mechanics that solitaire fans will recognize, but it gradually expands the experience with creative objectives and steadily increasing challenges. Every stage introduces unique card arrangements that require thoughtful planning rather than random clicking, encouraging players to carefully manage their available moves while making good use of boosters and collectible items. Coins earned throughout the adventure can be used to acquire useful tools that help overcome particularly difficult levels, adding a welcome layer of progression that rewards persistence. The adventure also includes side activities such as collecting hidden objects, helping various characters recover lost possessions, and unlocking achievements, which add variety between the core solitaire puzzles and help the campaign maintain its momentum.

The game's presentation is one of its strongest features. Drawing inspiration from the vibrant imagery associated with Día de los Muertos, every location is filled with colorful decorations, lively environments, and imaginative character designs that celebrate the holiday's festive atmosphere rather than focusing on horror. The art style successfully captures the balance between life and death, creating an inviting world that feels magical instead of intimidating. Soft background music complements the visuals nicely, providing a calm and relaxing soundtrack that fits the casual nature of the gameplay while making extended play sessions enjoyable.

Forgotten Tales: Day of the Dead also succeeds because it gives its adventure personality. Manuel's journey is populated by memorable characters, humorous encounters, and a straightforward romance that keeps the story moving forward. While the narrative does not attempt to deliver unexpected plot twists or emotional complexity, it serves its purpose well by connecting each new area and providing motivation to continue clearing increasingly difficult stages. This combination of storytelling and puzzle-solving helps distinguish the game from many other solitaire titles that rely solely on repetitive gameplay without offering a meaningful sense of progression.

The game is not completely free of drawbacks. Since the underlying mechanics remain faithful to classic solitaire, experienced players may eventually find that the gameplay loop becomes predictable despite the additional objectives and narrative elements. Certain late-game stages can also feel heavily influenced by card distribution, creating situations where success depends as much on favorable draws as careful strategy. Fortunately, the available power-ups and progression system help reduce frustration, allowing players to continue advancing without feeling permanently stuck.

Overall, Forgotten Tales: Day of the Dead is a polished and charming solitaire adventure that successfully combines familiar card mechanics with an appealing fantasy narrative and an attractive visual presentation. Green Sauce Games demonstrates that even a traditional genre can remain engaging when supported by colorful artwork, rewarding progression, and a world filled with personality. While it does not dramatically reinvent solitaire, it delivers exactly what it sets out to provide: a relaxing, entertaining, and content-rich adventure that will appeal to casual players, puzzle enthusiasts, and fans of story-driven solitaire experiences alike.

Rating: 6/10
